Messages.Author: Frederick Scott
Messages.Body:
"librarian" <auct...@superfuncards.com> wrote in message
news:lATRj.7215$DG....@newsfe10.phx...

> You steal an Imbued with Second Sight on it. You use it to get -1i for monsters (or whatever). I'm assuming the Second Sight
> goes back the original owner of the Imbued's asheap? Or does it go to your asheap?

The rule is, plainly, "When a card is 'burned', it is placed into its
owner's dicard pile...". (1.1, #2.) "In addition to their own effects,
conviction cards may be spent (_BURNED_) to pay the conviction costs which
some cards require." (Rule #2, Conviction, from the Nights of Reckoning
expansion page.) Emphasis on the parentheical "_BURNED_" mine but clearly,
playing a conviction card for its power requires burning it. The procedure
for burning a card is spelled out in rule 1.1., #2. I can see no other
interpretation.

Bleh. Time to put the rules for Imbued, convition cards, and powers
into the rulebook, don't you think? (I know it's work...)

Fred

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <lATRj.7215$DG....@newsfe10.phx>, librarian

<auct...@superfuncards.com> writes:
>You steal an Imbued with Second Sight on it. You use it to get -1i for
>monsters (or whatever). I'm assuming the Second Sight goes back the
>original owner of the Imbued's asheap? Or does it go to your asheap?

Cards going into ash heaps always go to the ash heap of the owner (i.e.
the person whose library/crypt they started in).

Ditto any cards that get shuffled into a library or crypt, or put on the
bottom of a library/crypt.
